# Stingerloom ORM

> Stingerloom is a TypeScript ORM for PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite on Node.js. Entities are defined with the decorator-free `defineEntity` builder, which infers the row type, or with decorators. It provides a typed query DSL without code generation, multi-tenancy scoped by AsyncLocalStorage, an opt-in Unit of Work, schema-diff migrations with a CLI, and a NestJS module.

- Package: `@stingerloom/orm` on npm, MIT license, current major version 3.x
- Runtime: Node.js 22 or later; CommonJS and ES module builds with type declarations
- Runtime dependencies: one (`sql-template-tag`). Database drivers and integrations are optional peer dependencies, installed only when used: `pg`, `mysql2`, `better-sqlite3`, `reflect-metadata`, `class-transformer`, `@nestjs/common` / `@nestjs/core`, `fast-glob`
- CLI: `npx stingerloom migrate:run | migrate:rollback | migrate:status | migrate:generate | introspect`
- Source: https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm
- Changelog: https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

**Verification.** CI runs on every pull request: the unit suite, SQLite integration tests, MySQL 8 and PostgreSQL 16 integration tests against real database servers, stress tests, a timezone matrix, a type check of every example project, and a check of the TypeScript samples in the documentation against the public API. In November 2026 the unit suite held about 7,000 tests and the SQLite integration suite about 2,100.

**Minimal example** (`npm install @stingerloom/orm reflect-metadata better-sqlite3`):

```typescript
import "reflect-metadata";
import { EntityManager, defineEntity, t, InferEntity } from "@stingerloom/orm";

export const Todo = defineEntity("todos", {
  id: t.int().primary().generated(),
  title: t.varchar(200),
  done: t.boolean().default(false),
  createdAt: t.datetime().createTimestamp(),
});
export interface Todo extends InferEntity<typeof Todo> {}

const em = new EntityManager();
await em.register({
  type: "sqlite", // "postgres" and "mysql" also take host, port, username and password
  database: ":memory:",
  entities: [Todo],
  synchronize: true, // for development; production schemas are managed with migrations
});

const todo = await em.save(Todo, new Todo({ title: "Ship it" }));
const open = await em.find(Todo, {
  where: { done: false },
  orderBy: { createdAt: "ASC" },
  take: 10,
});
await em.update(Todo, { id: todo.id }, { done: true });
await em.propagateShutdown({ closeConnections: true });
```

**Notes for writing code with Stingerloom:**

- Entities are written with `defineEntity` and the `t` field builders, or with decorators (`@Entity`, `@Column`, `@ManyToOne`, ...). Both produce the same metadata and can be mixed in one project. Decorators need `experimentalDecorators`, `emitDecoratorMetadata` and `import "reflect-metadata"`; `defineEntity` needs no compiler flags.
- Two `defineEntity` entities that reference each other break type inference unless one side names the row type and annotates the thunk, as in `t.oneToMany<Post>((): AnyEntityClass => Post, "author")`, and both row types are declared by interface merging (`export interface Post extends InferEntity<typeof Post> {}`).
- `em.find()` and `em.findOne()` take `where`, `relations`, `orderBy`, `take`, `skip` and `select`. A `select` narrows the result type.
- JOINs, grouping, window functions and computed expressions go through `em.createQueryBuilder(qAlias(Entity, "e"))`. The alias exposes each column as a typed property with operators such as `.eq()`, `.gt()` and `.in()`, so a misspelled column fails the TypeScript build.
- `synchronize: true` applies every column change, `"safe"` only creates tables and adds columns, and `"dry-run"` logs the DDL without running it. Production schemas are usually managed with `npx stingerloom migrate:generate` and `npx stingerloom migrate:run`.
- Multi-tenant code runs each request inside `MetadataContext.run(tenantId, async () => { ... })`. The `tenantStrategy` option chooses the isolation: `"search_path"` (default) and `"schema_qualified"` use a PostgreSQL schema per tenant, `"tenant_column"` filters by a tenant column on every database, and `"database"` gives each tenant its own database.
- Transactions use `em.transaction(async (txEm) => { ... })` or the `@Transactional()` decorator.
- The Unit of Work (identity map, dirty checking, batched flush) is opt-in: `em.extend(bufferPlugin())`, then `const buf = em.buffer()` and `await buf.flush()`.
- Each major version has an upgrade guide, and the changelog lists every breaking change together with the change it requires.

## Getting started

- [Getting Started](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/getting-started): Install, define a first entity, and run create/read/update/delete in about five minutes
- [Configuration](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/configuration): Every `register()` option, from a minimal setup to production settings
- [Upgrading to 3.0](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/upgrade-3.0): What changed from 2.x and what to update
- [Upgrading to 2.0](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/upgrade-2.0): What changed from 1.x and what to update

## Defining entities

- [Defining Entities](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/define-entity): The recommended code-first `defineEntity` API with `t` field builders and inferred row types
- [Entities & Columns (Decorators)](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/entities): Class-based entities with `@Entity`, `@Column` and the other decorators
- [Decorator-Free Reference](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/decorator-free): The decorator-free equivalent of every decorator, with runnable examples
- [Relations](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/relations): ManyToOne, OneToMany, OneToOne and ManyToMany, eager and lazy loading, and cascades
- [Inheritance Mapping](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/inheritance-mapping): Class hierarchies as single-table, joined (TPT) or table-per-class (TPC) tables

## Reading and writing

- [EntityManager CRUD Basics](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/entity-manager): The EntityManager, the entry point of every create, read, update and delete
- [Querying & Pagination](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/entity-manager-querying): Column selection, ordering, filtering, pagination, aggregates and EXPLAIN
- [Writes & Transactions](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/entity-manager-writes): Batch writes, upserts, transactions and raw SQL execution
- [Transactions](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/transactions): `em.transaction()`, `@Transactional`, isolation levels, savepoints and deadlock retry
- [EntityManager Advanced](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/entity-manager-advanced): Event listeners, subscribers, multi-tenancy, plugins, query diagnostics, repositories and graceful shutdown
- [Pagination & Streaming](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/pagination): Offset pagination, cursor pagination and streaming large result sets
- [Query Result Cache](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/caching): Opting individual reads into a short-lived result cache
- [Dates & Timezones](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/timezone): How temporal values are written and read on each database

## Query builder and SQL

- [Query Builder](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/query-builder): `SelectQueryBuilder` for the queries `find()` cannot express
- [JOINs](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/query-builder-joins): Joins written by hand or derived from relation metadata
- [QueryDSL Expressions](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/query-builder-querydsl): The `qAlias` typed expression chain: operators, functions, CAST, CASE, window functions
- [JSON Navigation](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/query-builder-json): Querying into JSON columns by path
- [Aggregations & Subqueries](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/query-builder-aggregations): GROUP BY, HAVING, subqueries and DISTINCT
- [Execution & Results](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/query-builder-execution): Ordering, pagination, locking, index hints, result validation and the methods that run a query
- [Patterns & Productivity](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/query-builder-patterns): Conditional building, reusable scopes and the other builder helpers
- [Raw SQL & CTE](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/raw-sql): `RawQueryBuilder` for CTEs, window functions and set operations
- [Typed Raw Rows](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/row-shapes): `defineRow` for typed reads of tables that have no entity
- [Raw Pipeline](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/raw-pipeline): Streaming raw rows in batches without entity transformation

## Schema and migrations

- [Migrations](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/migrations): Writing and running migrations, and generating them from a schema diff
- [Migration CLI](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/cli): The `stingerloom` command: `migrate:run`, `migrate:rollback`, `migrate:status`, `migrate:generate`, `introspect`
- [Seeding](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/seeding): Filling a database with initial or test data
- [Introspection](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/introspection): Generating entity code from an existing database

## Multi-tenancy and advanced features

- [Multi-Tenancy](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/multi-tenancy): Layered tenant metadata, `MetadataContext.run()`, the four tenant strategies and tenant provisioning
- [Advanced Features](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/advanced): Subscribers, N+1 detection, cursor pagination, validation, repositories, streaming, deadlock retry and operational settings
- [Events & Subscribers](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/events): Lifecycle hooks, event listeners and `EntitySubscriber`
- [Logging & Diagnostics](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/logging): Query logging, N+1 detection, slow-query warnings, EXPLAIN and query timeouts
- [Plugins](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/plugins): Extending an EntityManager with `em.extend()`
- [Write Buffer Basics](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/write-buffer): The Unit of Work: identity map, dirty checking, entity states and `flush()`
- [Write Buffer Advanced](https://biud436.github.io/stingerloom-orm/write-buffer-advanced): Lazy loading, pessimistic locking, bulk DML, flush events and modes, and nested units of work

## Examples

- [vanilla-todo-sqlite](https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/tree/main/examples/vanilla-todo-sqlite): `defineEntity` in a plain script, with no framework and no decorators, on in-memory SQLite
- [nestjs-todo](https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/tree/main/examples/nestjs-todo): Minimal NestJS CRUD
- [nestjs-todo-sqlite](https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/tree/main/examples/nestjs-todo-sqlite): Minimal NestJS CRUD on SQLite through `better-sqlite3`
- [nestjs-cats](https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/tree/main/examples/nestjs-cats): CRUD, relations, soft delete, cursor pagination and `EntitySubscriber`
- [nestjs-blog](https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/tree/main/examples/nestjs-blog): ManyToMany, upsert and soft delete, with e2e tests
- [nestjs-linear-clone](https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/tree/main/examples/nestjs-linear-clone): An issue tracker with recursive CTEs, window functions, `SKIP LOCKED` queues and optimistic locking
- [nestjs-multitenant](https://github.com/biud436/stingerloom-orm/tree/main/examples/nestjs-multitenant): PostgreSQL schema-per-tenant isolation with `TenantMigrationRunner`
